title: Control Plane Interaction Canvas
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working canvas to reason about how the control plane surface is split for routing decisions, orchestration responsibilities, and runtime adapter ownership across regions and deployment modes. Aim: produce a clear, implementable ownership map (who touches what) and a set of coordination rules for cross-team changes.

High-level goals:
- Minimize cross-team coupling for routine changes (deploys, feature flags, model swaps).
- Keep runtime-specific concerns (quantization, kernel selection) inside serving/runtime teams.
- Make routing policies declarative and centrally visible for audit and rollback.
- Ensure multi-region failover paths are explicit and testable.

Primary actors (informal):
- API Gateway team: external ingress, auth, rate limits, request-level routing to control plane endpoints.
- Control Plane Orchestration: policy engine, route decision logic, canary/circuit-breaker, rollout coordinator.
- Runtime Adapters: hardware-specific adapters that translate orchestration directives into runtime configuration (e.g., model variant choice, batch limits, affinity).
- Serving Runtime: the actual inference process (GPU pools), implements KV cache, batching, and low-level kernel use.
- Infra/SRE: region capacity, cluster health, failover mechanisms.

Canvas: key responsibilities (one-liners)
- API Gateway: tenant-facing entrypoint, API-level validation, primary auth, call-level metering, forward to control-plane endpoints. Not responsible for model-level capacity decisions.
- Policy Engine (Control Plane): owns routing decision graph (latency vs cost tiers), fallback chains, TTL for cached decisions. Exposes audit trail for decisions.
- Rollout Coordinator: owns canary/A-B rollout orchestration, policy triggers for rollback. Integrates with observability/quality signals.
- Adapter Boundary: owns translation from policy directives to runtime configs (e.g., "use quantized-ggml-x if region=apac and latencyBudget>80ms").
- Runtime: enforces adapter configs, reports telemetry, accepts model pinning requests, enforces per-tenant isolation constraints.
- Infra/SRE: capacity and region arithmetic; notifies control plane on region-level degradation; owns region-level failover execution (coordination with control plane for drift).

Routing policy primitives (proposed minimal set):
- priority (latency|cost|availability)
- allowed_variants: list of compatible model variants (highQuality, balanced, lowCost)
- region_preference: ordered list (home, nearby, fallback)
- autoscale_hint: concurrency and burst thresholds for dedicated pools
- ttl_seconds: how long a decision can be cached by API gateway or clients

Decision flow (happy path):
1) API Gateway receives request -> validates auth, rate-limit -> forwards to Policy Engine with metadata (tenant, route id, region, latency budget).
2) Policy Engine looks up route policy + runtime health -> picks target variant and region according to primitives -> emits decision + audit id.
3) Adapter consumes decision -> converts to runtime config (quantization profile, batch window, KV cache policy) -> sends to runtime pool or returns endpoint URL.
4) API Gateway receives final endpoint info and proxies traffic to runtime.
5) Telemetry from runtime + adapter flows back to control plane for continuous feedback.

Failure modes & ownership (short):
- Decision timeout at policy engine: control plane orchestration to return cached fallback; API Gateway to enforce client timeout and return 503 if no fallback.
- Runtime adapter mis-translate config: runtime team provides circuit-breaker to reject invalid configs; adapter team owns hotfixes and tests.
- Region outage: infra/SRE declares region degraded -> control plane shifts region_preference and triggers rollout to next region; API Gateway reroutes new requests based on updated policy.
- Stale policy cache on gateway: policy engine increases TTL or emits explicit invalidation event; API Gateway listens to invalidation stream.

Ownership matrix (quick, for discussion):
- Public ingress & auth: API Gateway team
- Per-tenant routing policy authoring: Platform (product + platform) but stored/served by Control Plane Orchestration
- Runtime variant implementations: Serving Runtime + Runtime Adapters (shared responsibility)
- Canary orchestration: Control Plane Orchestration (owner of orchestration code), Feature flags stored in product infra
- Rollback policies: Control Plane Orchestration + SRE for runbooks
- Observability: Instrumentation owned by runtime + adapters; dashboards owned by Console/Observability team; alerts owned by SRE

Multi-region coordination rules (draft):
- Single source of truth for policy (Control Plane). Any region-specific override must be explicitly scoped with expiration.
- Region health states: {healthy, degraded, offline} emitted by SRE. Control Plane must map these to routing changes via predefined policies (no manual scripts for fast path).
- Geo-affine preference: tenants can set home-region; policy engine will try home-region first unless degraded or cost constraint violates SLO.

Operational playbooks (starter):
- Model swap with canary across regions: orchestration triggers 5% traffic in home region -> monitor latency/error/quality signals -> expand to 25% -> if stable, expand to 100% -> if cross-region variance observed, pause and escalate to platform-engineering.
- Region failover drill: SRE flips region state to degraded in staging -> control plane re-routes and adapter logs must show config application; measure SLO impact and recovery time.

Open questions / decision items:
- Where should final endpoint resolution live: in policy engine (return endpoint URL) or adapter (return config then runtime allocates)? Tradeoffs: speed vs central control.
- Schema for "allowed_variants" -- canonical names and compatibility labels needed across runtime teams.
- Invalidation channel: real-time stream (Kafka) vs polling (cache TTL). Need an SRE cost estimate.
- How to test cross-region canaries without blowing quota/costs.

Next actions (short-term backlog):
- (Asha) draft canonical variant naming doc and circulate (due 2024-10-15).
- (Miguel) prototype a policy decision payload (JSON schema) that includes audit_id and ttl_seconds (due 2024-10-22).
- (Priya) run a small staged failover test with infra in staging and capture telemetry (due 2024-10-29).
- Review meeting: platform-engineering sync to walk canvas and lock ownership (proposed 2024-11-05).

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally informal — expect iterations. Please comment inline with: missing responsibilities, unclear edges, and any regulatory constraints that would force model pinning inside a specific region. Also list any dependent tickets (GH/Jira) so we can link in the final ownership map.
